quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic to protect yourself.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Changing lanes quickly to get through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with reckless, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on the road or crossing. Be extra careful where children are present. Always give pedestrians the right of way at crosswalks.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clean.
Leave more space between your vehicle and the cars ahead.
Be cautious around all vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snowy weather, keep your windshield and mirrors clean. Increase the space behind the car in front of you. Slippery roads make it harder for your vehicle to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: When slow driving blocks the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Cannot exit the freeway.
Can continue through or exit from your current lane.
Can stay in your lane and continue through the interchange.
Must exit if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means your lane will not continue forward. It will become an exit ramp. If you are in this lane, you can change lanes to go through, or you must exit the highway.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: Where should you go to take the Missouri driver exam?

options.text: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
Any Department of Transportation office.
Any Missouri contract office.
The nearest high school driver education class.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any Missouri State Highway Patrol testing station.
questions.explanation: The Missouri State Highway Patrol gives the driver exam. Contact the Highway Patrol or the Department of Revenue to find the testing center closest to you.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You may drive around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised at a railroad crossing:

options.text: As long as a train is not too close.
If your vehicle does not damage the gate.
If you look carefully in both directions first.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are all the way up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with motor vehicles and bicyclists.

questions.question: SATOP stands for:

options.text: Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.
Salt And Tar On Pavement.
Steer At The Other Point.
Stop Airing Tires Over Pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program.
questions.explanation: SATOP stands for Substance Abuse Traffic Offender Program. Completing this program is required for people convicted of alcohol-related driving offenses.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake steadily. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Not turn on any vehicle lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic and within 500 feet of vehicles you are following. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
Entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions less than perfect, drive below the speed limit. Even at the posted speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road intersects with a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roadways separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a crossbuck sign, you should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue if a flagger clears you to do so.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, obey all their instructions.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
You must drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs can prohibit certain actions. These signs are rectangular, white, with red and black markings. A red circle with a slash through a symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass, even if dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions may pass. You may only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How should you let others know you want to be an organ donor?

options.text: Fill out the organ donor section on the back of your license.
Tell your family about your decision.
Have two witnesses sign the back of your license.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To make sure people know you want to be an organ donor, complete the back of your license, tell your family, and register online or in person when you apply for or renew your license.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and check for nearby police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: Anytime.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see well, pull over and stop until it gets better.
